breakfast.name: Ćevapi with Somun
instructions: Mix meat with grated onion, garlic, baking soda, salt, pepper
Knead well, rest 2 hours in fridge
Shape into small finger-sized sausages
Grill over charcoal until done
Serve in split somun with raw onion and kajmak
breakfast.description: Grilled minced meat sausages in flatbread — Bosnia's most famous dish.

breakfast.name: Burek
ingredients: For filling: 500g ground beef, 2 onions, salt, pepper
instructions: Sauté meat with onions until cooked
Roll phyllo thin, spread filling in strip
Roll into long coil, spiral into baking pan
Brush with oil
Bake at 180°C 45 min until flaky and golden
Serve with yogurt
breakfast.description: Flaky spiral phyllo pie filled with spiced meat.

breakfast.name: Somun sa Kajmakom (Flatbread with Cream)
instructions: Warm somun bread
Split open while hot
Spread generous layer of kajmak inside
Eat immediately — the warmth melts the kajmak
breakfast.description: Warm Bosnian flatbread stuffed with kajmak cream — the simplest and best breakfast in Sarajevo's baščaršija.

breakfast.name: Ćevapi for Breakfast (Full Plate)
instructions: Grill ćevapi over charcoal until charred and juicy
Split somun bread
Tuck ćevapi inside
Pile raw diced onion on top
Add a generous scoop of kajmak
Serve with ajvar on the side
This is breakfast, lunch, and dinner — the meal that put Sarajevo on every food list
breakfast.description: Yes, Bosnians eat ćevapi for breakfast — and it went viral when food creators showed the 9am meat-finger-in-bread ritual. The queues at Željo or Petica in Sarajevo start at dawn. The most Instagrammed food in the Balkans.

lunch.name: Begova Čorba (Bey's Soup)
instructions: Boil chicken with vegetables until tender
Remove chicken, strain broth
Shred chicken
Make roux with butter and flour
Add sour cream and egg yolks
Stir into broth, add chicken
Heat gently, don't boil
Garnish with parsley
lunch.description: A creamy, velvety chicken soup from Ottoman Bosnian tradition.

lunch.name: Bosanski Lonac (Bosnian Pot)
instructions: Layer meat and vegetables alternately in clay pot
Season each layer with garlic, peppercorns, bay leaf
Add vinegar and water to just cover
Cover tightly, bake at 160°C for 2 hours
Do not stir — layers develop flavor
Serve from the pot
lunch.description: A slow-baked layered meat and vegetable pot — never stirred.

lunch.name: Klepe (Bosnian Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: 300g ground beef, 1 onion (finely diced), salt, pepper
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Mix filling: raw beef with finely diced onion, salt, pepper
Roll dough thin, cut squares
Place filling on each, fold into triangles, press edges
Boil in salted water until they float, then 3 more min
Serve in bowl with garlic yogurt
Drizzle paprika-infused melted butter over top
lunch.description: Bosnian meat dumplings in garlic yogurt with paprika butter — Bosnia's version of manti, a legacy of Ottoman cuisine.

dinner.name: Klepe (Bosnian Dumplings)
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, 1 egg, water, salt
Filling: 400g ground beef, 1 onion, salt, pepper
Topping: garlic yogurt sauce, paprika butter
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Mix beef with onion and seasoning
Roll dough thin, cut squares
Fill and fold into triangles, press edges
Boil in salted water 15 min
Top with garlic yogurt and paprika-infused butter
dinner.description: Meat-filled dumplings topped with garlic yogurt and paprika butter.

dinner.name: Japrak (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
instructions: Blanch grape leaves
Mix beef, rice, onion, paprika, salt, pepper
Place filling on each leaf, roll tightly
Pack into pot seam-down
Add water and lemon juice to cover
Simmer 60 min
Serve with sour cream
dinner.description: Bosnian-style stuffed grape leaves with paprika-spiced filling.

dinner.name: Bosanski Lonac (Bosnian Pot)
instructions: Layer in heavy pot: onion, meat, vegetables, meat, vegetables
Tuck in garlic, peppercorns, bay leaf
Add vinegar and enough water to barely cover
Seal pot tightly (traditional: dough seal around lid)
Cook on very low heat for 2+ hours — do not open or stir
The layers stay distinct, the broth concentrates
Serve from the pot at the table
dinner.description: A sealed layered pot of meat and vegetables — never stirred, slow-cooked for hours. Bosnia's defining one-pot dish, ancient and unchanged.

snacks.name: Pita Zeljanica (Spinach Pie)
instructions: Wilt spinach, squeeze dry, chop
Mix with feta, eggs, onion
Layer phyllo in pan with oil
Spread filling between layers
Bake at 180°C 40 min until golden and flaky
snacks.description: Flaky phyllo pie filled with spinach and cheese.

snacks.name: Ćevapi with Somun
instructions: Mix meat with grated onion, baking soda, salt, pepper
Refrigerate 2 hours or overnight
Shape into small finger-sized links
Grill over charcoal, turning once
Serve 10 pieces in split somun with raw diced onion and kajmak
snacks.description: Bosnia's most famous food — small grilled meat fingers in flatbread with onion and cream. Sarajevo's ćevabdžinicas have served them for centuries.

desserts.name: Tufahije (Poached Apples)
ingredients: Syrup: 2 cups sugar, water, lemon juice
instructions: Make syrup, poach apples until tender
Fill centers with walnut-sugar mixture
Place in serving dish, pour syrup over
Top with whipped cream
desserts.description: Whole apples poached in syrup and filled with walnuts.

desserts.name: Tufahije (Poached Stuffed Apples)
ingredients: Walnut filling: walnuts, sugar, lemon zest
instructions: Core apples, keeping bottom intact
Poach in sugar syrup until tender but holding shape
Fill centers with ground walnut mixture
Return to syrup, simmer 5 more min
Serve in syrup bowls topped with whipped cream
desserts.description: Apples poached in syrup and stuffed with walnuts — an Ottoman-era Bosnian dessert served at every kafana.

drinks.name: Bosanska Kafa (Bosnian Coffee)
instructions: Heat water in džezva (cezve)
When bubbles form, remove, add coffee
Return to heat, let foam rise
Remove before boiling over
Let grounds settle
Pour into fildžan cups, serve with sugar and rahat lokum
drinks.description: Bosnian coffee — a ritual with its own etiquette.

drinks.name: Šljivovica (Plum Brandy)
instructions: Pit and crush plums
Let ferment naturally 3-4 weeks
Distill twice over copper still
Age in oak barrels 2+ years
Serve as digestif
drinks.description: Traditional plum brandy — the king of Balkan spirits.

drinks.name: Bosanska Kafa (Bosnian Coffee)
instructions: Heat water in džezva (copper pot) until it begins to rise
Remove, add coffee, stir once
Return to heat, let foam rise — do not boil
Remove when foam crests
Pour slowly into fildžan cups, foam first
Serve with sugar cube and rahat lokum on the side
drinks.description: Not Turkish coffee — Bosnian coffee. The ritual matters: the džezva, the foam, the sugar cube bitten between sips. A daily act of hospitality.
